management_notes: Founded by Peter Marrone, former Yamana Gold CEO who built Yamana from a small-cap to a $5B+ producer. Management team carries deep gold sector operating experience across West and East Africa. Insider ownership has been bolstered through the Sadiola acquisition. Minor deduction for running concurrent multi-jurisdiction projects (Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Ethiopia) which stretches operational bandwidth.
geology_notes: Sadiola is a long-producing gold system previously operated by AngloGold Ashanti and IAMGOLD — well-documented mineralisation with a track record of steady production. The Kurmuk development project in Ethiopia adds exploration upside. No measured or indicated resource estimate is present in the extracted filings data for this run; reserve summary text was extracted as a truncated sentence fragment and does not convey usable figures. Scoring reflects known production profile rather than a current resource statement.
capital_notes: 125.9M shares issued and outstanding; 136.6M fully diluted. The ~8.5% dilution from options, RSUs, and convertible debentures is moderate for a mid-tier producer. No warrants were identified in filings. Convertible debentures (equivalent to ~6.2M shares) represent the most material overhang. RSUs (2.2M) and options (2.4M) are modest relative to share count. No flow-through financing was detected in filings, consistent with an Africa-focused issuer. RSU and convertible instrument types are excluded from share_instruments per schema constraints; their dilutive effect is captured in shares_fully_diluted.
catalyst_notes: Production ramp-up at Sadiola following restart is the primary near-term catalyst; quarterly production results will set market tone. The Kurmuk project in Ethiopia (development stage) provides medium-term upside if permitting and construction remain on track. Sadiola's deep sulphide expansion adds longer-dated optionality. No company-transforming news is expected in the immediate quarter.
acquisition_notes: Mid-tier African gold producers trade at material discounts to NAV given political risk premiums. Mali (military junta since 2021, strained Western relationships, ongoing security concerns in the Sahel) and Ethiopia (recent Tigray civil conflict, political volatility) both carry elevated jurisdiction risk that compressed P/NAV multiples well below 1.0x in comparable transactions. Sadiola was acquired from the prior owners at a distressed multiple — potential re-rating requires sustained production and political stability.
analyst_summary: Allied Gold is a credible mid-tier producer built by a management team that has done it before. The Sadiola mine is a known, producing asset, and Kurmuk provides genuine optionality. The stock is held back by the twin jurisdiction risks of Mali and Ethiopia — both of which have seen government instability that creates headline risk regardless of mine-level execution. Investors who already hold West African exposure or who want a management-quality bet at a discount to African peers will find this interesting; risk-averse retail investors should wait for clearer political resolution in Mali. Resource data was not extractable from the filings for this run; reserve summary text was incomplete. Confidence is low pending updated resource statement.
